coverage.scope: Mapped passages are correspondences, not sentence-level formal support. Section-passage overlaps are document structure, not claim or proof implications. Unmapped text and passages omitted by the selector remain in the validated paper. Graph records outside the selected prerequisite closure remain in the bundle and are not asserted absent. Argument links combine recorded Lean references, curated support, formalization correspondence and explicit assumptions; their SCCs describe only that mixed recorded reachability. Reading order and platform decomposition are separate.

treatments.rationale: Derives nonnegative tail cost and its vanishing on the support by feasible atom addition and compact fractional mass removal. The first-variation formula and regularity are cited inputs, and the sign conclusion uses minimality.

Derives the value and slope conditions from derivatives of the contact function, with a separate right-hand expansion at zero. The origin argument retains contact at zero when zero belongs to the support and the zero-field identity q(0)=0.

States the quantitative curvature estimate for any admissible positive plateau and applies it together with minimiser contact to exclude a bounded gap. The estimate is an imported input here; its nonminimiser scope does not supply contact.

Derives the bounded-gap contradiction by integrating the endpoint-chord bound for q prime. Contact and the imported curvature estimate have separate roles; the initial and terminal cases are treated separately in the same passage.

Develops smoothness from the quotient of moments before differentiating, then transfers the quantitative spatial-moment inequality through local constant replacements at a fixed interior time. Compact-strip stability is a cited input; positivity is asserted only for 0<t<1, and the argument does not transfer third time derivatives or add formal acceptance.

Derives the continuous-coefficient fixed-time inequality by admissible local constant replacement and common-strip convergence of spatial moments, then applies it after q=t. Minimality is unnecessary for the transfer itself.

Explains the terminal-gradient martingale and displays the cancellation that gives the scalar value identity, with endpoint and covariance justifications delegated to the cited source and long record. This use needs the full-support moment identities, not positive density.

States the accuracy-dependent finite deterministic depth and angles before the size limit, and outlines the additional synthesis, seed-removal and fixed-word transfer steps. The passage routes the complete construction elsewhere and gives no depth rate, finite-size rate or efficient angle-selection guarantee.
States the finite adjacent-correlation limit and explains normalization, mean-preserving rounding, l2 error control and the mesh-before-cutoff order; full estimates remain in the long record.

Explains the first-chaos coefficient of the parent coordinate and its pairing with the generating child direction, including the zero independent-root-seed contribution. The source theorem supplies the full rooted construction.

reading_links.rationale: Develops the smoothness and fixed-time local-replacement arguments that the exposition names as further reading. Both treatments retain interior-only strict positivity and separate this ordinary argument from formal-check status.

Expands the terminal-gradient and scalar-value pointer with the martingale limit, integral cancellation and source destinations. The short passage also has further topics; this link concerns its scalar-value treatment, not equivalence of the whole passages.

Adds the theorem quantifiers, order of limits and circuit-stage outline to the exposition reference. It remains an outlook with a destination for the full construction, rather than a complete circuit proof.

meaning: Document structure and authored passage correspondences. Reading order, containment and text overlap do not assert mathematical dependencies. Source text and support record bodies are fetched separately.
